title: Malaysia Lifts Serian Emergency Declaration as Haze Lingers at 'Very Unhealthy' Levels
detail: Malaysia's King Sultan Ibrahim consented to lift the state of emergency for Sarawak's Serian district on Sept. 7, five days after declaring it when Serian's API hit a hazardous 519-521. The decision followed advice from Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and Sarawak Premier Abang Johari Openg, based on agency reports showing Serian's API had fallen below the hazardous (300+) threshold to 222 by Monday morning. A Prime Minister's Office statement said the federal and state governments would keep closely monitoring the situation and urged residents to keep limiting outdoor activity. Despite the lift, air quality remained compromised through the day: Serian's API climbed back to 245 (very unhealthy) by 2pm, and 11 areas statewide — including Sarikei (193), Kuching (192), Sri Aman (184), Mukah (182), and Sibu (182) — registered unhealthy readings, while Samarahan stayed in the very-unhealthy band. The 647 Sarawak schools ordered closed through Sept. 11 remained shut.

media.caption: Aerial view of thick haze over Serian, Sarawak, days before Malaysia lifted its emergency declaration

title: Panama Canal Administrator Says Rio Indio Project Will End Drought-Driven Draft Cuts — But It's 5-6 Years Away
detail: Panama Canal Authority Administrator Ilya Espino de Marotta said on Sept. 7 that the Rio Indio water-supply project, once complete, 'will guarantee that the canal won't have to resort again to either draft reductions or transit reductions' during dry periods — but cautioned the infrastructure is five to six years from completion. The comments came as the canal continues operating under El Niño-driven drought restrictions: daily transit slots were cut Sept. 3 (Neopanamax to 9, Panamax to 25, falling to 23 on Sept. 15) and a further Neopanamax draft reduction to 47.5 feet, originally set for Oct. 1, remains postponed at the current 48.0-foot limit. Espino de Marotta said the Authority may need to impose additional restrictions in the near term if rainfall over the next three months fails to lift reservoir levels in the Gatun watershed.

media.caption: The Panama Canal Authority says the Rio Indio project will end future drought-driven transit and draft restrictions once complete in 5-6 years
